note: Relationship health score tunables (issue #383, ADR-0023). Hand-authored, not generated — mirrors backend/internal/perfbench/testdata/budgets.json's pattern: every number carries a mandatory reason, changing a number is a deliberate reviewed edit. Loaded/validated by backend/internal/scoring.LoadConfig at every call site (services.ComputeAllContactScores); config.go's validate() also drift-checks this file's closeness_tiers against the live relationship_type_registry.go.

weights.reason: Time since the last qualifying interaction is the single strongest, least gameable signal of relationship health — weighted highest.
A single recent interaction after a long gap shouldn't look identical to a steadily-maintained relationship; frequency catches that.

Structural distance (relationship type / hop count) sets expectations — a stranger and a spouse shouldn't be judged by the same bar — but it's not itself a maintenance signal, so it's weighted equal to frequency, not higher.
A pending, unreviewed reach-out suggestion is a real but narrow warning signal (org/title/address change only) — enough to matter, not enough to dominate.

Record-editing activity is a weak proxy for relationship health (editing a phone number isn't interacting with someone) — lowest weight, deliberately capped influence (see ADR-0023's documented gaming-vector note).

thresholds.reason: moss >= 70, chanterelle 40-69, russula < 40. Roughly even thirds of the scale, with chanterelle the widest band since 'drifting' covers more real situations than either extreme.

sibling_of.reason: Close family, typically less contact-dependent than immediate household ties.

partner_of.reason: Unmarried romantic partner — as close as spouse_of but kept a separate tier since the registry itself treats it as a distinct, non-projecting type.

friend_of.reason: Core social relationship this app is built around maintaining.

roommate_of.reason: Regular proximity, not necessarily emotional closeness.

co_parent_of.reason: Significant coordination relationship, not necessarily personal closeness.

owned_by.reason: Pet-ownership structural edge, not a person-to-person closeness signal.

owns.reason: Pet-ownership structural edge, not a person-to-person closeness signal.

related_to.reason: Deliberately vague fallback token (migration/legacy data) — no closeness can be inferred from it.

immediate.reason: Immediate family/household — short expected check-in window.

close.reason: Close friends/partners — monthly is a reasonable default cadence.

distant.reason: Structural but low-closeness edges (pets, unspecified legacy relations).

unknown_closeness.reason: No self-contact set, or the contact isn't reachable in the graph at all — genuinely unknown, not 'distant': a flat midpoint that neither rewards nor penalizes the common case of a user who has never wired themselves into the relationship graph (see ADR-0023 — this is expected to be the most common branch in practice). The 90-day default interval is deliberately the longest of any tier, since there's no basis to expect frequent contact.

recency.reason: no_interaction_value=45 is deliberately in the chanterelle band but well above 0 — a contact with zero recorded history isn't proven neglected, but shouldn't score as healthy either; it is a fixed constant, not derived from the target interval, so a same-day-created contact doesn't coincidentally match '1 day overdue'. overdue_ratio_cap=2.0 means a contact exactly at its target interval scores 50 (midpoint) and one at double the interval bottoms out at 0.

frequency.reason: A 6-month trailing window is long enough to smooth out a single recent interaction after a long gap, short enough to still reflect current behavior rather than a relationship's entire history.

closeness.reason: A structural 2-hop path (e.g. your spouse's friend) starts at 60 — below the closest direct tiers but clearly above 'unknown' — and decays 15 per additional hop, floored at 20 so a very distant but still-structurally-connected contact never reads as fully unknown.

reach_out.reason: Deliberately in the russula band on its own — an unreviewed suggestion is a concrete, actionable warning, not a mild ding — but the 15-point weight still lets strong Recency/Frequency/Closeness outweigh it rather than veto the score outright.

last_updated.reason: Same 6-month window as frequency for consistency. Floor of 30 (not 0) keeps this the weakest possible drag on the total score, matching its lowest-of-five weight — editing a contact record is at most weak evidence of engagement.
